predictions: P-A (Ep track, falsifiable): the fresh blind engine returns a MONOTONICALLY SOFTENING Ep across the pulse — first-block (~1.2-4.4 s) Ep >= last-block (~15-21 s) Ep, with the peak-region (~4-15 s) Ep landing in 130-200 keV, straddling the GBM catalog's peak-flux COMP Ep = 155.4 +- 16.1 keV and integrated COMP Ep = 161.4 +- 9.5 keV after frame alignment (catalog Ep is nuFnu-peak, 10-1000 keV, dets n0n1n9b1, interval -7.168->33.792 s — WIDER than ours, so a small downward pull on the catalog value from the soft tail is expected, not a discrepancy). Independent support: the catalog's own peak-bin index (-0.486 +- 0.162) is harder than its integrated index (-0.926 +- 0.054) at ~2.6 sigma. FALSIFIER: last-block Ep exceeds first-block Ep at >2 sigma, or any block's Ep falls outside 40-400 keV.

P-B (BB / union rule, falsifiable): the L18+ engine returns ZERO blocks passing the union rule ((LRT_BANDBB_BAND>=9.2 & kT>1.05) OR (LRT_CPLBB_CPL>=9.2 & kT>1.05)) — i.e. bn120130938 stays OUT of the significant-BB population. The archival maximum is LRT = 5.04 (blk0, CPL+BB baseline, kT = 11.08 keV), only ~55% of threshold. FALSIFIER: >=1 block passes the union rule. If it does, the falsification is INFORMATIVE rather than embarrassing — the pre-L18 engine under-detected BB (BB seed-poisoning + Ep-cap lessons L8/L9), so a fresh pass is EXPECTED to move upward, never downward. A fresh union count of 0 confirms the null; a count of 1 (most likely blk0, kT ~ 10-13 keV) confirms the L8/L9 correction; a count >= 2 would say the archival BB null was a wholesale engine artifact and the census lower-limit is looser than assumed. Note blk0's BANDBB_VALID=False vs CPLBB_VALID=True: this is a live BASELINE-DEPENDENCE instance (T8 twin / union-rule fix) and the fresh run must report the margin against a NAMED baseline, never 'the' dAIC.

P-C (break structure, falsifiable): ZERO blocks show a valid second break — no block reaches LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 with DSBPL_VALID=True. Archival max = 2.36 (integrated). FALSIFIER: any block with LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 and DSBPL_VALID=True; that would make this burst a NEW two-break candidate found only after the L18-L20 hardening, which is exactly the class the campaign exists to find.

P-D (model decisiveness, falsifiable and the most likely to be interesting): the fresh run is again MODEL-INDECISIVE at the ddAIC >= 10 doctrine level in every block. Archival AIC margins are 0.02 / 1.01 / 0.61 / 0.83; the GBM catalog independently shows red-chi2 spread <= 0.002 across COMP/Band/SBPL on the integrated spectrum, with Band beta unconstrained (-3.543 +- 384.3). Two independent pipelines, two decades of method apart, both fail to discriminate. PREDICTION: the fresh integrated fit ALSO fails to constrain beta (relative error > 50%), and the AIC winner in every block wins by dAIC < 10. FALSIFIER: any block where a model wins by dAIC >= 10, or where beta is constrained to better than 30%. If falsified, the gain came from the ENGINE (multistart / cap / coverage fixes), not from the data — and that is a headline result for the agentic paper, because there is no literature for this burst that could have leaked the answer.

P-E (window coverage, methodological): whatever the fits say, the analysis covers -3.0 -> +26.0 s while the catalog T90 spans -5.12 -> +33.79 s. PREDICTION: the emission omitted at both ends is low-flux tail (the n9 light curve is back to baseline by ~+35 s and the T50 interval [4.10, 13.31] s sits comfortably inside our window), so our integrated Ep should sit at or slightly ABOVE the catalog integrated Ep = 161.4 keV, not below. FALSIFIER: our integrated Ep comes out significantly BELOW the catalog value, which would mean the omitted tail is not what we think it is and the window must be revisited before any census use.
